scenes.title: DROP TABLE
scenes.narration: DROP TABLE permanently removes a table and every row it contains, so use it with care.

scenes.title: Removing a table
bullets: Removes all rows along with it
Cannot be undone without a backup
scenes.narration: DROP TABLE deletes the table's structure as well as all of its data. Both the definition and every row disappear together in one action. Because this is not something you can casually reverse, it demands caution.

scenes.title: Dropping a table safely
scenes.narration: This statement removes the temp_report table from the database. The IF EXISTS clause prevents an error if the table is already gone. That makes the command safe to run in scripts that may execute more than once.

scenes.heading: DROP vs TRUNCATE
scenes.narration: DROP TABLE eliminates the table entirely, leaving nothing behind to reuse. TRUNCATE instead clears all rows but keeps the empty table in place. Choose DROP when the table is no longer needed and TRUNCATE when you only want to empty it.

scenes.text: DROP TABLE is irreversible, so confirm backups before removing production tables.
scenes.narration: Treat DROP TABLE as a permanent action and confirm you have backups before removing any table that holds real data.
